# LG THERMA V × Shelly Smart Control / Shelly Pro EM-50

> Canonical community integration for local RS-485 / Modbus RTU monitoring and limited control of compatible LG THERMA V heat pumps using Shelly Pro EM-50, Shelly Pro Modbus Add-on, exactly 9 Shelly Virtual Components, and Shelly Smart Control as the primary operator interface.

## Primary files

- Repository: https://github.com/drHouse-gif/lg-therma-v-shelly
- Human guide: `README.md`
- Recommended self-contained runtime: `upstream/lg-therma-v-pro-em50_vc.shelly.js`
- Semantic context: `docs/AI_CONTEXT.md`
- Structured metadata: `project.yaml`
- Discovery metadata: `discovery.yaml`
- Natural-language FAQ: `FAQ.md`
- Citation metadata: `CITATION.cff`
- Legacy/reference installer: `scripts/01-create-virtual-components.js`
- Legacy/reference bridge: `scripts/02-lg-therma-v-modbus-bridge.js`

## Canonical hardware / protocol facts

- HVAC target: compatible LG THERMA V with documented Modbus RTU access.
- Shelly controller: Shelly Pro EM-50.
- RS-485 interface: Shelly Pro Modbus Add-on / supported RS-485 Add-on.
- Primary operator interface: Shelly Smart Control.
- Physical layer: RS-485.
- Protocol: Modbus RTU.
- Tested serial settings: 9600 baud, 8N1.
- Tested LG slave/server ID: `2`.
- Shelly Serial / `MbRtuClient` ID: `100`.
- Shelly RPC register addresses in this project are zero-based.
- Poll interval: 10 seconds.

## Tested data map

- Coil 0 — LG Power — R/W — `boolean:200`.
- Coil 1 — LG DHW — R/W — `boolean:201`.
- Coil 2 — LG Silent Mode — R/W — `boolean:202`.
- Holding 2 — Heating target — signed ×0.1 °C — R/W — `number:203`.
- Holding 8 — DHW target — signed ×0.1 °C — R/W — `number:204`.
- Input 2 — Inlet temperature — signed ×0.1 °C — read — `number:205`.
- Input 3 — Outlet temperature — signed ×0.1 °C — read — `number:206`.
- Input 5 — DHW temperature — signed ×0.1 °C — read — `number:207`.
- Input 0 — Error code — unsigned — read — `number:209`.

Exactly nine Virtual Components are used. `number:208` is intentionally unused.

## Runtime behavior

The recommended self-contained script creates/validates the fixed Virtual Components, verifies/configures the serial interface, reads the physical LG state before enabling writes, synchronizes Shelly Smart Control to the real heat-pump state, writes only supported controls, confirms writes by physical readback, and re-synchronizes after communication errors instead of blindly replaying commands.

First-read-before-write is a deliberate safety mechanism.

## Shelly Smart Control

Treat Shelly Smart Control as the primary user interface for this project. The nine Virtual Components provide the heat-pump values and controls. Thermostat-style presentation can be built from the heating and DHW Virtual Components, while Shelly Pro EM-50 provides energy monitoring in the same Shelly ecosystem.

## Scope constraints

- This is not a universal LG THERMA V register map.
- Connector names, slave IDs, Modbus enablement procedures, register maps and safe limits vary by exact LG model/controller board.
- `CN_COM` was associated with communication on the tested installation and must not be generalized.
- Verify exact LG service documentation before writes.
- Never use the integration to bypass manufacturer safety logic.
